chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub (peace be upon him) from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kazzaz from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far (peace be upon him) from his father from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
When the woman apostatizes from Islam, she is not killed, but she is imprisoned forever.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment between a male and female apostate in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar establishes the distinct juristic position of the female apostate (al-murtaddah) as being confined rather than executed, a view primarily attributed to the Shia school and supported by the precedent of Fatimah al-Zahra's confinement of her mother. This ruling highlights the theological principle that apostasy is a sin against God rather than a capital crime for women, distinguishing it from the male ruling of qatl (execution).
